label: Heart rate and resting heart rate
measured_in_space: Yes. Chest strap or wrist sensor, continuously; resting value taken during sleep.
why: The earliest general sign that the body is under load: infection, dehydration, poor sleep and stress all raise resting heart rate.
hazard_effect: Without gravity, body fluid shifts toward the head and blood volume falls, so the heart adapts and deconditions. The same exercise slowly costs more heartbeats.
escalate: Tell the CMO if resting heart rate stays above your own normal for several days, or reaches 100 bpm at rest. 120 bpm at rest: flight surgeon now.
prevention: Daily aerobic and resistive exercise, enough fluid and salt, protected sleep.

label: Blood pressure
measured_in_space: Yes. Automatic arm cuff, taken seated and at rest.
why: Shows how hard the heart and vessels work and whether the body has enough circulating fluid.
hazard_effect: Fluid shift and a smaller blood volume change pressure regulation; after landing, standing up can cause fainting.
escalate: Systolic 160 mmHg or more at rest, or below 90 mmHg: stop activity and contact the CMO and flight surgeon.
prevention: Exercise, hydration, salt and fluid loading before return to gravity.

label: Blood oxygen (SpO2)
why: Tells whether the lungs and the cabin air deliver enough oxygen.
hazard_effect: A closed habitat depends on life support: a leak, a pressure change or an oxygen-system fault shows up here.
escalate: Below 94 %: re-seat the sensor and repeat. Below 90 %: oxygen mask and flight surgeon now.
prevention: Cabin oxygen and pressure monitoring, prompt leak checks.

label: Breathing rate
why: Rises early with fever, low oxygen or high CO2.
hazard_effect: CO2 can pool around a crewmember in still air because warm air does not rise without gravity.
escalate: A sustained rise with headache or breathlessness: check cabin CO2 and tell the CMO.
prevention: Good airflow in every module, especially sleep stations.

label: Body temperature
measured_in_space: Yes. Ear or forehead thermometer; skin patch for continuous reading.
why: Fever is the clearest sign of infection.
hazard_effect: The immune system is weakened by stress, radiation and poor sleep, and a closed cabin spreads germs easily. Dormant viruses can reactivate.
escalate: 38.0 C or more: rest, fluids, recheck every 2 hours and inform the CMO. 39.0 C or more: flight surgeon now.
prevention: Hygiene, clean shared surfaces, sleep, nutrition, pre-flight quarantine.

label: Blood sugar (fasting glucose)
measured_in_space: Yes. Finger-prick meter, in the morning before eating. In this demo the values are simulated from published ranges.
why: Shows how the body handles energy. Both low and high values impair thinking and performance.
hazard_effect: Less muscle and less activity reduce insulin sensitivity; irregular meals and limited food on long missions add to it.
escalate: Below 70 mg/dL: take fast sugar and recheck. Below 54 mg/dL or 250 mg/dL and above: flight surgeon now. 126 mg/dL or more on two mornings: CMO review.
prevention: Regular meals, exercise, enough protein, logging what you eat.

label: Daily sleep hours
measured_in_space: Yes. Wrist sensor plus a morning check-in.
why: Sleep protects attention, mood and the immune system. Short sleep is a leading cause of errors.
hazard_effect: No natural day and night, noise, workload and, on Mars, a 24 h 40 min day shift the body clock.
escalate: Under 6 hours for several nights, or with slow reaction time: move safety-critical tasks and inform the CMO.
prevention: Fixed sleep schedule, dim light before sleep, bright light after waking, quiet dark sleep station.

label: Mood, stress and fatigue check-in
measured_in_space: Yes. A 20-second self-report each morning: the same 1-5 scales as the real PMData study.
why: Behavioural health problems build slowly and people under-report them. A daily score makes a slow change visible.
hazard_effect: Months in a small space with the same few people, far from family, with delayed communication.
escalate: Mood 2 or lower for three days, or mood, stress and sleep worsening together: talk to the CMO; a private medical conference can be arranged.
prevention: Exercise, family contact, meaningful work, shared meals, private time.

label: Cabin CO2
measured_in_space: Yes. Cabin sensors and personal monitors. The demo values are simulated from real ISS measurements (NASA OSDR EDA).
why: High CO2 causes headache, tiredness and poorer thinking, which can be mistaken for illness.
hazard_effect: A sealed cabin only stays breathable while the scrubbers and fans work.
escalate: 1-hour average above 3 mmHg, or 7-day average above 2.5 mmHg with headache or fatigue: ventilate first. Above 6 mmHg: leave the module.
prevention: Airflow checks, scrubber maintenance, avoiding crowding in one module.

label: Radiation dose
measured_in_space: Yes. Area monitors and personal dosimeters. The demo replays real measurements from Curiosity's RAD instrument on Mars (NASA/JPL).
why: Dose adds up over a career and raises cancer risk; a solar storm can deliver a large dose within hours.
hazard_effect: Beyond Earth's magnetic field, galactic cosmic rays are constant and solar particle events arrive with little warning.
escalate: Dose rate at twice the normal level or more: whole crew to the storm shelter. Career dose near 600 mSv: mission planning with the flight surgeon.
prevention: Shielded shelter, limiting EVA during solar activity, tracking every crewmember's dose.

radiation_msv.dataset: NASA/JPL MSL RAD x quality factor 3.0, replayed

label: Bone and muscle
measured_in_space: Partly. Exercise minutes and exercise heart rate daily; bone density by scan before and after flight; ultrasound in flight.
why: Without loading, hip bone density falls about 1-1.5 % per month and muscles shrink, which raises fracture risk on landing.
hazard_effect: Weightlessness removes the daily load that keeps bone and muscle.
escalate: Exercise below target for a week, or exercise heart rate drifting up: review the prescription with the CMO.
prevention: Resistive exercise six days a week, aerobic exercise, protein and vitamin D.

label: Reaction time (PVT)
why: An objective check of alertness before safety-critical work.
hazard_effect: Sleep loss, high CO2 and workload slow reactions before a person notices.
escalate: Much slower than your own normal: hand over EVA, robotics or docking tasks.
